ages.title: Upcoming age milestones

what.40: Long-term care premiums start (no filing needed).
what.60: If pay drops on re-employment after retirement, consider same-day loss and re-acquisition to lower the standard remuneration immediately.
what.65: Long-term care premiums stop (moves to the municipal care insurance; no filing needed).
what.70: Pension coverage ends. No filing if pay is unchanged (handled by the Japan Pension Service); otherwise file the Report of Worker Attaining Age 70 (70歳到達届) within 5 days.
what.75: Health coverage ends (moves to the late-stage elderly medical system). File the Coverage-end Report (資格喪失届) within 5 days. Dependents need to join another plan such as National Health Insurance.

ages.effectNote: Born on the 1st, so the age is treated as reached in the previous month ({{y}}-{{m}}).
ages.empty: No one reaches a milestone in this period.
ages.hint: Only current employees are shown. Ages 40, 65 and 75 apply to health insurance members; age 70 to pension members. Filings are a guide.

pension.60: Pension: the special old-age employees' pension (paid before 65) applies only to men born on or before April 1, 1961 and women born on or before April 1, 1966 with at least one year of employees' pension coverage. Others receive it from 65 (early receipt is possible if they choose). Eligible people receive a claim form from the Japan Pension Service three months before their starting age.
pension.65: Pension: old-age basic and employees' pensions start at 65. A claim is required; the Japan Pension Service sends the claim form 3 months before the 65th birthday, and it can be submitted from the day before the birthday (unclaimed amounts may be lost after 5 years). Please inform the employee.

specificOfficeHow.manual: (Uses the company-wide count entered in the office settings.)

text.myNumberCheck: The employee submitted a My Number. Show all digits, check them against the ID documents, then register or return it.
text.myNumberDispose: Two years have passed since losing coverage ({{date}}). The retention period for health insurance and pension documents (two years from completion) has ended, so dispose of the My Number. If you count completion from the date of the pension service's notice, wait two years from that date and dismiss this with “Checked”.
text.contractEnd: The employment contract ends on {{date}}. If it is renewed, register the next contract; if not, enter the retirement date (this leads to the loss-of-coverage To-do). If it renews automatically on the same terms, check and then dismiss with "Checked".
text.contractEndNotice: Because the contract has been renewed 3 or more times or the employee has worked for more than 1 year, advance notice must be given by {{noticeBy}} if it will not be renewed (MHLW standards on fixed-term contracts, Article 2).
text.contractEndShort: This is a contract of 2 months or less. Once it is expected to continue beyond 2 months through renewal, the employee becomes subject to social insurance from that point.
text.officeNameAddress: The office name/address was changed on {{date}}. File the "Change (correction) of name/address of the covered office" within 5 days of the change (if the office moved outside the jurisdiction, file with the pension office for the previous address).
text.officeRelation: Office information was changed on {{date}}. File the "Change (correction) of office-related information" within 5 days of the change (for a change of employer etc., also write the previous information).
text.address: The address changed on {{date}}. Automatic updates through the link between My Number and the basic pension number may not apply to this person, so check whether the "Insured person address change notification" is needed and, if so, file it promptly.
text.addressKumiai: The address changed on {{date}}. Some health insurance societies require a separate address notice. Check the society's rules.
text.cardReturn: Coverage ends (ended) on {{date}}. This person was issued an eligibility certificate (shikaku kakunin-sho), so collect it and return it with the loss-of-coverage notification (Kyokai Kenpo). If it cannot be collected, attach the "Notice of inability to collect the eligibility certificate". Dismiss with "Checked" once collected.
text.loseDeath: This is a loss of coverage due to death. The loss date is the day after the date of death, and the notification is due within 5 days. Collect and attach the eligibility certificate if one was issued. If the person had dependents, they also lose dependent status, so guide them to switch to National Health Insurance etc.
text.retireGuide: Retires on {{date}}. Explain health insurance and pension after retirement to the employee.

retireVoluntary.kyokai: Voluntary continuation: if the employee submits the application to the Kyokai Kenpo branch of their prefecture by {{deadline}} (within 20 days from the day after retirement), they can stay covered for 2 years. The premium is paid entirely by the person (standard monthly remuneration capped at 320,000 yen). National Health Insurance or becoming a family member's dependent are other options. For pension, if there is no next employer, enroll in the National Pension at the municipality. Dismiss with "Checked" after explaining. For employees joining National Health Insurance, provide a document showing the date coverage ended (such as a certificate of loss of coverage) if requested.
retireVoluntary.kumiai: Voluntary continuation: if the employee applies to the health insurance society by {{deadline}} (within 20 days from the day after retirement), they can stay covered for 2 years (premium paid entirely by the person; check the society's rules). National Health Insurance or becoming a family member's dependent are other options. For pension, if there is no next employer, enroll in the National Pension at the municipality. Dismiss with "Checked" after explaining. For employees joining National Health Insurance, provide a document showing the date coverage ended (such as a certificate of loss of coverage) if requested.

text.retireNoVoluntary: Voluntary continuation is not possible because the person was not continuously covered for 2 months. Guide them to National Health Insurance or becoming a family member's dependent. For pension, if there is no next employer, enroll in the National Pension at the municipality. Dismiss with "Checked" after explaining. For employees joining National Health Insurance, provide a document showing the date coverage ended (such as a certificate of loss of coverage) if requested.
text.name: The name changed on {{date}} (the registered name has been updated). Automatic updates via the link between My Number and the basic pension number may not apply to this person, so check whether the "Insured person name change notification" is needed and, if so, file it promptly.

dependentChange.increase: On {{date}}, the employee applied saying a family member may become a dependent. Check eligibility; if so, register them on the dependents card and file the Dependent Change Report within 5 days (for a spouse, the National Pension Category 3 notification uses the same form).
dependentChange.decrease: On {{date}}, the employee applied saying a dependent may no longer qualify. Enter the end date on the dependents card and file the Dependent Change Report within 5 days. Collect the eligibility certificate if one was issued.

text.overseasCertificate: The Japanese certificate of coverage for the assignment in {{country}} expires on {{date}}. To continue the assignment, apply for an extension before it expires (the other country must approve). Otherwise, the employee returns to Japan or switches to the local system (if the Japanese company stops paying salary, a loss-of-coverage notification is also needed in Japan). Once the extension certificate is issued, enter the new end date and this item disappears.
text.overseasPayAbroad: Assigned to {{country}} since {{date}} and paid only by the overseas company, but still insured in Japan. If the Japanese company bears no salary (such as a family allowance at home), the employment relationship is regarded as ended and a loss-of-coverage notification is needed (the loss date is usually the start of the assignment). If you confirm that the Japanese company bears salary and coverage continues, dismiss with "Checked".
text.myNumberCheckFamily: {{family}} family member number(s) have been submitted. Show all digits in the family My Number section, check them, and approve or return.
text.myNumberDisposeFamily: {{family}} family member number(s) also remain. Dispose of them as well.
text.officerCheck: Coverage of a part-time officer cannot be decided. Answer the six items (regular attendance, other jobs, board meetings and so on).

ratesMissing.kyokai: The Kyokai Kenpo rates from March {{year}} are not registered in the app yet. Until they are, premiums from March are calculated with the previous year's rates (the rates are decided around February each year and apply from March premiums, paid in April). Please check them against the notice from Kyokai Kenpo. Once checked, you can hide this with "Checked".
ratesMissing.kumiai: The health insurance society's rates from March {{year}} are not registered yet. When the rate notice arrives from the society, register it from "Insurer and location history" in the office settings (the month of revision differs by society). If the rates do not change, you can hide this with "Checked".

text.adjustmentDeadline: The deadline to apply for the premium adjustment scheme ({{date}}) is approaching. To use it, submit the application to the pension office by the deadline and tick "Use the premium adjustment scheme" in the office settings. If you decide not to use it, you can hide this with "Checked".

insurerChange.toKumiai: From {{month}}, the health insurer changes from Kyokai Kenpo to "{{to}}". What the company usually does: (1) apply to join the health insurance society and submit the employees' and dependents' information; (2) collect the eligibility certificates issued by Kyokai Kenpo and return them; (3) check that the new eligibility certificates or eligibility notices have been issued; (4) ask whether the society decides the standard monthly remuneration again on joining.
insurerChange.toKyokai: From {{month}}, the health insurer changes from "{{from}}" to Kyokai Kenpo. What the company usually does: (1) complete the loss of coverage with the health insurance society and collect and return its eligibility certificates; (2) file the health insurance enrollment and dependent change reports with the pension office (check the deadline with the pension office); (3) check that the new eligibility certificates or eligibility notices have been issued.
insurerChange.kumiaiToKumiai: From {{month}}, the health insurer changes from "{{from}}" to "{{to}}". What the company usually does: (1) complete the loss of coverage with the previous society and collect and return its eligibility certificates; (2) apply to join the new society and submit the employees' and dependents' information; (3) check that the new eligibility certificates or eligibility notices have been issued; (4) ask whether the standard monthly remuneration is decided again on joining.

text.insurerChangeCommon: Documents and deadlines differ by insurer, so follow the new insurer's instructions. Employees' pension coverage continues (no filing needed). Premiums keep using the current grades. Dismiss with "Checked" when done.
text.bonusNone: Bonuses are scheduled for {{month}}/{{year}}, but none are recorded. If none were paid, submit a "Bonus non-payment report" to the pension office by {{date}} (end of the following month; also to the health insurance society if applicable). If they were paid, record them and this item disappears. Once submitted, you can hide it with "Checked".
text.bonusReport: A bonus was paid on {{date}} ({{count}} people). Submit the bonus payment report to the pension office within 5 days of the payment date (also to the health insurance society if you use one). Include people aged 70+, people whose premiums are exempt and people who lost coverage that month. Once submitted, choose "Checked" to hide this.
text.acquireReport: Coverage started on {{date}}. Submit the acquisition report to the pension office within 5 days of that date (also to the health insurance society if you use one). If there are dependents, submit the dependent change report with it. Once submitted, choose "Checked" to hide this.
text.lossReport: Coverage ended on {{date}}. Submit the loss report to the pension office within 5 days of that date (also to the health insurance society if you use one), with any collected eligibility certificate. People who lose health insurance at 75 also need this report. Once submitted, choose "Checked" to hide this.
text.bonusCumulative: Including the previous employer, the cumulative standard bonus amount for health insurance in fiscal {{year}} is {{total}} yen, above the cap ({{cap}} yen). For the cap to apply, the employee must submit a "Cumulative standard bonus declaration" to the insurer (follow the insurer's instructions). The app already applies the cap. Once you have informed the employee, you can hide this with "Checked".
text.birthDate: The date of birth was corrected on {{date}}. If the acquisition notification was already filed, promptly submit a "Date of birth correction notification". Age thresholds (long-term care at 40/65, 70, 75) may change, so check premiums and filings too.
text.actualHours: Actual working hours in the pay for {{first}} and {{second}} were {{h1}} and {{h2}} hours a week, at or above the threshold ({{limit}} hours) for two months in a row. Even if contracted hours are below it, if this continues or is expected to, coverage starts on {{date}} (the first day of the third month). Review the contract or file an acquisition notification. If it was temporary, hide it with "Checked".
text.acquireAmount: The fixed wage paid in {{month}} ({{fixed}} yen) is higher than the monthly remuneration on the acquisition notification ({{reported}} yen). Allowances such as commuting or housing that started late still belong in the acquisition amount: correct the expected pay in the contract and file a correction (put catch-up payments back in the months they belong to). If this is a raise decided after acquisition, hide it with "Checked".
text.childcareSpecial: Raising a child under 3 since {{child}}; the pension standard monthly remuneration from {{month}} ({{now}} yen) is below the month before ({{base}}: {{pre}} yen). If the employee applies, premiums stay the same but the future pension uses the earlier amount. Tell the employee and mark as checked once the application is submitted.
text.dependentReport: Dependents changed on {{date}}. Submit the Dependent (Change) Notification within 5 days to the pension office (or to the health insurance society). For a spouse, the National Pension Category 3 notification uses the same form. Dependents added on the date of acquisition are submitted together with the acquisition notification. Mark as done once submitted.

hint.optIn: For short-time workers with a minimum wage reduction permit (specified reduction special cases): the date the Japan Pension Service accepted their request to enroll. Coverage starts on this date.

hint.collection: Choose this, for example, to have only employees on unpaid leave pay in cash.
hint.foreign: Enter the nationality as an ISO 2-letter code (Vietnam VN, China CN, Philippines PH, Germany DE, etc.). While a certificate of coverage under a social security agreement is valid, the employee may not be enrolled in Japanese insurance.
hint.roman: Enter as on the residence card. Converted to capitals.

hint.filingName: Choose the name written on the related filings. This name is shown in the app and on filings.
hint.sortByKana: Check for people who use a Japanese surname, to list them under あ–わ.
hint.needsRomanNameFiling: Required with the Application to Enroll (資格取得届) when the person has no My Number or it is not linked to the basic pension number. Checked automatically for people without resident registration.
hint.residenceCard: Number at the top right of the residence card (2 letters, 8 digits, 2 letters)
hint.optOut: For specified reduction special cases: the date the Japan Pension Service accepted their request to withdraw. Coverage ends the next day (health and pension are requested together; the employer's consent is not needed).
hint.multipleOffices: An employee working at two or more offices chooses the managing pension office with a notification, and the premiums are split by each office's pay. The premiums in the app are an estimate using only this office's pay. Check the amounts in the notice from the pension office (the split is not calculated by the app).
hint.emergency: Who the company contacts in case of an accident or sudden illness (up to 2). Enter separately from the employee's own phone.

retireReason.transfer: For a transfer, enter the last day worked at the previous office as the retirement date. The loss-of-coverage date becomes the next day (the day of the transfer).
retireReason.death: The loss-of-coverage date is the day after the date of death. File the loss notification within 5 days.

hint.address: The address on notifications is the one in the resident register. If the person lives somewhere else, also enter the place of residence below.
hint.overseas: On notifications, write the country and city, e.g. "Living in London, UK".
hint.addressFactDate: If an address change notification is needed, it appears in the To-do list. It is needed for people whose My Number is not linked to their basic pension number, people living overseas, short-stay foreign nationals, people with health insurance only, and people registering a place of residence.

todo.title: To-do list (start here every morning)
todo.body: Items that may need a filing are listed by urgency (now, coming up, missing information). Applications to Enroll (資格取得届), Coverage-end Reports (資格喪失届) and category changes can be handled from the to-do item in a small window. Saving records the enrollment and the filing and removes the item. Age milestones and similar items can be marked as checked and restored from "Show checked".

acquire.title: When someone joins (Application to Enroll, 資格取得届)
acquire.body: Register the employee and add an employment contract to see their insured category (e.g. short-time worker). If they should be insured but are not, the to-do list shows an Application to Enroll. Enter the enrollment date, monthly remuneration and grades in the window. The Standard Monthly Remuneration (SMR) decided on enrollment is saved at the same time.

loss.title: When someone leaves (Coverage-end Report, 資格喪失届)
loss.body: Entering a retirement date fills in the coverage-end date (the next day) and the reason. If a contract change means the person is no longer insured, open the Coverage-end Report window from "Review enrollment" in the to-do list. Reaching age 75 can also be filed from the age milestone item.

payroll.title: Entering payroll
payroll.body: On the payroll screen, enter the amount paid in money, fixed wages and payment basis days for each month paid. These are used for the annual SMR determination (定時決定) and SMR revisions (随時改定). You can also import them by CSV. "Also enter in-kind pay and details" shows the in-kind, total and retroactive pay columns. For one person and one month, you can also use "Enter a month" on the employee page. Enter in "retroactive pay" only differences from raises decided retroactively. Allowances paid late because of a late application or a mistake go back into the month they should have been paid (that month becomes the start month for a revision). Mark "prorated" for months where a mid-period hire, transfer or new allowance means a full month was not paid (that month is not used as a start month; counting begins the next month). Payment basis days are calendar days for monthly pay, days worked for daily pay, and total hours ÷ daily scheduled hours for hourly pay. For months where a retroactive pay cut was deducted, enter the amount before the deduction. One-off or up-to-three-times-a-year payments (e.g. a sign-on allowance or year-end allowance) do not go into payroll; register them as bonuses (bonus payment report). Monthly allowances go into payroll even if they share a payslip line with such payments.

inKind.title: Remuneration provided in kind (housing, dormitories, meals)
inKind.body: On the payroll month screen, press "Also enter in-kind pay and details" and open "Calculate" in the in-kind column. Values are converted to yen with the amounts set by the Minister of Health, Labour and Welfare for each prefecture. Meals are 0 yen if the employee pays two-thirds or more; housing is the value minus what the employee pays. Moving in mid-month is prorated. The prefecture of the workplace defaults to the office and can be changed.

regular.title: Annual SMR determination (定時決定, Remuneration Report)
regular.body: For employees on July 1 each year, the SMR from September is set from the average pay in April, May and June. Months with fewer than 17 payment basis days (11 for short-time workers) are excluded. From June to August, a link appears under the to-do list.

irregular.title: SMR revision after a pay change (随時改定, Remuneration Change Report)
irregular.body: When fixed wages change and the average of the three months from that month moves the SMR by two grades or more (one grade at the upper or lower limit), the SMR is revised. Candidates appear on the revision candidates screen from payroll, together with revisions after maternity or childcare leave.

leave.title: Premium exemption for maternity and childcare leave
leave.body: Adding leave from "+ Add" on the employee page exempts both shares from the month the leave starts to the month before the month containing the day after it ends. Childcare leave that ends within the same month is exempt if it lasts 14 days or more.

care.title: Periods without long-term care premiums (exemption)
care.body: Even at ages 40 to 64, people who moved overseas (removed from the resident register) or entered an exempt facility do not pay long-term care premiums. Adding a period from "+ Add" on the employee page removes the care share from that month automatically. A training or business trip of about a month does not qualify unless the person is removed from the resident register.

agreement.title: Social security agreements (foreign nationals)
agreement.body: People sent from an agreement country who hold a certificate of coverage are not enrolled in the Japanese pension (and, for some countries, health insurance). Entering the certificate country and period in the employee edit screen adds agreement checks and certificate expiry items to the to-do list.

csv.title: Importing CSV, Excel and PDF files
csv.body: Employees and payroll can be imported from CSV, Excel or PDF files. This app's template CSV goes straight to the review screen. Files with different headers, such as files exported from payroll or HR software, go through the "Match columns" screen, where you check which column goes to which field. Fields missing from the file can be filled with "Same value for everyone". Japanese era dates (R8.4.1) and Excel dates are read, and half-width katakana is converted to full width. Shift_JIS CSV saved from Excel can also be read.

myPage.title: Employee My Page and requests
myPage.body: Create an invitation link from "Personal info" on the employee page and send it to the employee. On My Page, employees can see their premium breakdown, answer requests and apply for changes such as their address. Answers and applications are reviewed under "Requests"; approving writes them to the employee record (with change history). To invite several people at once, select them in My Pages > Invites and accounts, press "Invite", and export the links as CSV (only people with a contact email; no email is sent automatically).

roles.title: Roles (administrator, general, employee) and the representative
roles.body: Administrators can register, edit, file and invite. General users can only view, and cannot see contact, commute and bank details or change history. Employees see only their own information on My Page. One administrator is the representative; only the representative can make other administrators general or remove them (so administrators cannot remove each other). Staff invitations are created under Members, and only someone who verifies the invited address can join. Administrators and general users can delete their own account at the bottom of Account settings (this cannot be undone). Owners must transfer the owner role first.

annual.title: Annual average (insurer calculation)
annual.body: If overtime and similar pay rise (or fall) at the same time every year because of the nature of the business or department, the standard monthly remuneration can be set by the annual average with the employee's consent. The app compares the regular average with the annual one (July to June for the annual determination; for monthly changes, the 3-month fixed-wage average plus the 12-month non-fixed average) and shows a candidate when they differ by 2 or more grades (1 grade near the upper or lower limit). Check "seasonal" and "consent" on the annual determination or revision page to apply it. One-off raises, a temporarily busy period, commuting allowance changes and the end of maternity or childcare leave are not eligible. Write "年間平均" in the remarks and attach the statement and consent form (every time).

filings.title: Filing lists (CSV for copying)
filings.body: In "Filing lists", choose a form (acquisition, loss, annual determination, monthly change, bonus payment) and a period, then press "Show" to list one person per row in the order of the form's numbered fields. Dates are in the Japanese era. You can also export CSV. My Number and address are not included. Remarks only include what the app records, so add anything missing. This is not the electronic submission format.

premiumList.title: Premium list marks (advance, 2+ offices)
premiumList.body: "Check advances" reads the pay for the deduction month and marks employees whose pay (cash) is less than their share with "Advance" and an estimated amount. The company pays it in advance and collects it later (the app does not record collection). "2+ offices" marks employees working at two or more offices; their premiums are split by the pension office, so the amounts are estimates. Check the notice.

display.title: Display (colors, menu, input)
display.body: Choose Light, Dark or Auto (follow the computer) in Settings > Appearance at the top right. Press the orange square at the top left to collapse the left menu to icons and widen the content. Both are remembered by the browser. In the payroll month and bonus tables, Enter and arrow keys move between cells (Enter moves to the next field in the employee form).

payrollSoft.title: Split with payroll software (export and cross-check)
payrollSoft.body: Payroll software calculates the deductions; this app is the master record of grades, rates and filings. On the premium list, “CSV for payroll software” exports employee numbers, standard monthly remuneration, care insurance, the employee share and the pay month for the deduction, for import into the payroll software. “Check deductions” reads the deductions file the payroll software produced; after matching the columns it compares them with the app's employee shares and lists only the people with differences or who could not be matched. Health etc. is compared as health insurance plus care insurance.

myNumber.title: My Number (register, request, dispose)
myNumber.body: Numbers are stored encrypted and never kept on screen or in Firestore. On the employee's Personal info tab, register the number yourself or ask the employee to provide it (they submit it from My Page; you show all digits, check them against the ID documents, then register or return it). Showing all digits and exporting require your password again, and views, registrations and disposals are logged. Two years after a departed employee loses coverage, a disposal to-do appears. For CSV, use the My Number column in the employee import, or “Import My Numbers (for registered employees)”.

childcareSpecial.title: Childcare period special rule (pension)
childcareSpecial.body:
If the standard monthly remuneration of someone raising a child under 3 falls below the month before they started raising the child, they can apply so that premiums stay at the lower amount while the future pension uses the earlier amount (Employees' Pension Insurance Act Art. 26). Fathers are eligible too. It appears in the To-do list as "Childcare period special rule (pension)".

■ What to submit
The childcare period special rule application, submitted by the company to the pension office.

■ Attachments
- Family register extract showing the relationship (original). Not needed if the company checks it and ticks "confirmed", or if both My Numbers are written (review may then take about a month)
- Residence certificate showing the child's birth date and that they live together (issued within 90 days, original). Not needed if both My Numbers are written

■ Months covered
- From the month the child was born (or raising started, for adopted children) to the month before the child turns 3
- Up to two years back from the month before the application
- Compared with the standard in the month before raising started (if not insured then, the latest month within the prior year; ask about the previous employer)

■ Applying again
The rule ends when an exempt childcare or maternity leave starts; apply again after the leave. Also apply again after changing jobs.

■ Children the app finds
From leave records (birth date on maternity leave, child's birth date on childcare leave) and dependents with the child relationship. Children recorded in neither (e.g. a spouse's dependent) are not found, so check with the employee.

special.title: Special revision (medical care, childcare or nursing care)
special.lead: When someone's pay drops sharply because work is adjusted (shorter hours, less overtime) to balance it with medical care, childcare or nursing care, and the standard monthly remuneration is expected to stay at least two grades lower for three months or more, it can be revised with the employee's written consent from the month after the filing month, using the pay of the filing month (for pay from {{start}}). Unlike an ordinary revision, it does not wait three months. When the adjustment ends and the grade rises by two or more, file promptly to revise it back.

special.note: Applying saves the standard remuneration from the revision month (reason: special revision) and a record. It appears in the monthly change list in Filings in the special-revision layout (first month in the third row). Health insurance and pension are filed at the same time (also to the health insurance society if any). Attach the statement and consent form every time, and keep it with the supporting documents for two years from the filing date. People revised in July–September are excluded from that year's annual determination.

If the direction is unclear (e.g. fixed wage down while a variable allowance starts in the same month), choose "direction to confirm" (proposed automatically when the fixed wage rises and overtime drops to zero). Candidates are recalculated from three months starting with the added month.
